issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1(iii) existentially introduces only C, theta, and sigma, but the level set L(x) in (Lev_set), on which the KL inequality (KL_y) is required, is defined using an additional constant gamma that is never introduced or quantified anywhere in the paper. Later text explicitly treats gamma as a constant 'given in Assumption 1' (e.g., (Phi_smooth_constants) and the input line of Algorithm 3), which the assumption does not do. As stated, the paper's central assumption is not a well-formed mathematical statement: the meaning of L(x), of the KL condition, and of every gamma-dependent quantity (e.g., r = gamma*epsilon^sigma/(4 L_f)) is undetermined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add '$\gamma > 0$' to the existentially quantified constants in Assumption 1(iii) (i.e., 'there exist constants $C>0$, $\theta\in[1/2,1)$, $\gamma>0$, and $\sigma>0$ ...'), making L(x) and all subsequent uses of gamma well-defined; no proof changes are required.
issues.overall_effect: The local KL assumption, which is the hypothesis of all main results, is ill-defined as written; Theorems 1, 4, 5 and Lemmas 4, 5, 9, 10, whose statements or proofs involve gamma or the level sets L(x), are undetermined until gamma is declared.
issues.title: Undefined constant gamma in the local KL assumption
issues.why_classification: The single forced correction (declaring gamma a positive existential constant of the assumption) is local and routine; the method, all conclusions, rates, and advertised scope survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1(iii) requires the KL inequality (KL_y) for every x in Omega, where Omega is open and must strictly contain X = dom p whenever dom p is not open. For x in Omega \ X, the paper's conventions give partial p(x) = empty, hence partial Psi(x) = empty and dist(0, partial Psi(x)) = infinity, so L(x) = {y : 0 < F*(x) - F(x,y)} is the entire suboptimal set and the assumption demands the KL inequality for ALL suboptimal y, i.e., a global KL condition at every such x. The paper's motivating Example (X = [1,2], q the indicator of [pi/4,pi]) fails the global KL at every x > 0 (at y = pi one has dist(0, grad_y phi - N_{[pi/4,pi]}(pi)) = 0 while the gap is positive), and every admissible open Omega containing [1,2] contains points outside X; hence the Example does not satisfy Assumption 1(iii) under any valid Omega. The Remark's claim that the Example satisfies 'the local KL condition' (condition (KL_y) of Assumption 1(iii)) is therefore false, and the intro's description, that the KL is assumed 'for each fixed outer variable x in dom p', misdescribes the formal assumption, which is materially stronger (a global KL in y is required for all x in Omega \ dom p). The theorems themselves remain valid under the stated, stronger assumption.

failure_location.quote: For example, the minimax problem in Example~\eqref{example} satisfies the local KL condition but not the global one.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Least severe complete resolution: keep Assumption 1(iii) as stated and correct the scope claims (Remark, intro, abstract), noting that the assumption additionally imposes a global KL in y for every x in Omega \ dom p and that the motivating Example is therefore not covered. Alternatively, restate Assumption 1(iii) for x in dom p only, which requires nontrivial proof adjustments (the openness of U_epsilon in Lemma 6 and the proof of Theorem 1, which applies the KL at points of U_epsilon that may lie outside X).
issues.overall_effect: The paper's scope claims are unreliable: the advertised weakening of the global KL assumption, and in particular the claim that the motivating Example is covered by the paper's local KL condition, do not match Assumption 1(iii), which excludes the Example and any problem whose inner maximization fails a global KL at points just outside dom p. The complexity guarantees (Theorems 4-5) remain valid under the assumption as stated.
issues.title: KL assumption demanded for all x in Omega degenerates to a global KL off dom p, so the motivating example is not covered
issues.why_classification: The complexity theorems survive unchanged, but a substantive advertised claim, namely that the motivating Example and similar local-KL problems satisfy the paper's assumption, is false and must be withdrawn (or the assumption restated with nontrivial proof rework); this limited weakening of scope, leaving a recognizably comparable result, exceeds a routine local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: dom F(x,.) = dom q and X = dom p, and neither domain is closed in general under Assumption 1(ii): a proper closed convex function can have a non-closed domain (e.g., q(y) = -log y on (0, infinity), whose epigraph is closed). The proof of Lemma 4 (lem:QG) asserts 'notice from Assumption 1 that dom F(x,.) is closed', an assertion the assumption does not support, in order to place the limit point y* of {Y(t_k)} in dom F(x,.); without it, y* may lie on a missing boundary of dom q where F(x,y*) = -infinity, breaking the upper-semicontinuity argument that y* is in Y*(x) and hence the growth bound (lem4_QG). Symmetrically, the proof of Lemma 6 (lem:open) asserts 'the closedness of X' to conclude that the limit x of a sequence from C lies in X; if dom p is not closed, x can lie outside X where dist(0, partial Psi(x)) = infinity, so x is not in C and the closedness of C, and with it the proof that U_epsilon is open, fails as written. Both proofs thus rely on an omitted hypothesis (closedness of dom p and dom q) that is never established.

failure_location.quote: In addition, notice from Assumption \ref{ass:Lip_Smo_KL} that $\dom\,F(x, \cdot)$ is closed.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis that dom p and dom q (i.e., X and Y) are closed to Assumption 1(ii); both proof steps then become valid with no other changes. Alternatively, replace the two steps with a contained argument showing that the relevant limit points must lie in the domains (the values and subgradients of a closed convex function blow up at missing boundary points, contradicting the finite limits established in the proofs).
issues.overall_effect: The growth property (Lemma 4), the error bound (Lemma 5), the openness of U_epsilon (Lemma 6), and hence the local Holder smoothness of F* (Theorem 1) and the entire complexity analysis of Algorithm 3 (Lemmas 9-10, Theorems 4-5) rest on the unestablished closedness of dom q and dom p.
issues.title: Proofs of the growth lemma and the openness lemma rely on unjustified closedness of dom q and dom p
issues.why_classification: The least severe complete resolution adds one standard local condition (closed domains of p and q) to the assumption, or an equally contained boundary argument, with no change to the method, conclusions, rates, or advertised scope (all examples in the paper use closed domains).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $h(z^0)-h^* \leq \delta$ and $\{h(z^\ell)\}$ is nonincreasing, it follows that $h(z^{k+1})-h^* \leq \delta$.
Suppose that $\{(x^\ell,y^\ell)\}^{k}_{\ell=0}$ are generated by Algorithm \ref{algo_implement:whole} for some $k \geq 1$ such that $x^{\ell} \in \cX^\rc_\epsilon$ for all $0\leq \ell < k$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3 (thm:subsolver_iters) is stated for Algorithm 2, whose input contract requires z^0 in {z : h(z) <= h* + delta}; its proof uses h(z^0) - h* <= delta both for the KL recursion and for the final bound (h-opt). In Lemma 9's proof, Theorem 3 is invoked for the subsolver call producing y^ell (initial point z^0 = y^{ell-1}, h = -F(x^ell, .), delta = gamma*epsilon^sigma), but the required condition F*(x^ell) - F(x^ell, y^{ell-1}) <= gamma*epsilon^sigma is never verified: it is not part of the lemma's hypotheses (iterates generated, x^ell in X^c_epsilon for ell < k) nor derived in its proof. The derivation of (opt-x-ell), and hence of the inexactness bounds (lem9-ineq1-1) and (lem9-ineq1-2), is therefore unsupported as written. The missing condition is derivable, and in Theorem 4's proof it appears as (F-x-ell) via the L_f-Lipschitz continuity of F* and F(., y) plus the previous output bound, but only inside an induction that itself relies on Lemma 9, so the lemma must be restated with this hypothesis or the induction restructured to carry it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Lemma 9 the hypothesis that the subsolver calls are admissible (F*(x^ell) - F(x^ell, y^{ell-1}) <= gamma*epsilon^sigma for 1 <= ell <= k), and in Theorem 4's induction verify it via the already-derived inequality (F-x-ell) (2 L_f ||x^{ell+1} - x^ell|| plus the previous gap bound is at most gamma*epsilon^sigma), carrying it as part of the induction hypothesis; all conclusions and rates are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The inexactness bounds on the inner iterates (Lemma 9), the descent lemma and stationarity bound (Lemma 10), and the iteration and first-order oracle complexity guarantees of Theorems 4 and 5 rest on an invocation of Theorem 3 outside its hypotheses.
issues.title: Lemma 9 applies the subsolver theorem without verifying its initial-point hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The repair adds a standard local hypothesis to Lemma 9 and reorders the existing induction in Theorem 4's proof using an inequality already derived there; no new lemma, construction, or rate change is needed, and every substantive claim and guarantee survives.
